statement: I- fits observed game I/O: no game far call to System:020e, and enabling I adds a check after each I/O operation.
L cannot be recovered from this EXE: L+ and L- produce identical EXE bytes without /V.
N is unconstrained where no floating operation is linked; N+ leaves the integer probe identical. SAM links no real-arithmetic runtime group.
No overlay machinery is needed to reproduce SAM; O+ alone does not change an ordinary EXE, so the permission flag is not recoverable.
R- is required by the complete Pack and BitBtn matches; R+ adds checks and changes their lengths.
S- is required by ordinary matched game routines; S+ adds stack-check calls. An interrupt prologue alone does not establish S.
V is not identifiable for valid same-capacity calls. V+ rejects string[20] passed to var string; V- accepts it.
Canonical effective memory settings are M 16384,0,655360; allocation is rounded to paragraphs, so the exact source literal for heapmax is not unique.
EXE code order is program then reverse unit initialization order; initialization follows dependency-first uses traversal, with shared dependencies initialized once.
Retained Pascal routine bodies follow definition order, not interface declaration order; forwards permit moving helper bodies after a target.
Unused Pascal routines and their literals/typed constants are dropped. Linked runtime groups can retain unused entrypoints together.

statement: Pascal unit init follows retained Pascal bodies, but linked external object code can follow init.
A routine string literal is emitted in CS immediately before its body; literal bytes may make the first public offset nonzero.
Retained typed constants, including routine-local typed constants, occupy initialized DS, not CS. Unused typed constants can disappear.
Initialized DS blocks precede uninitialized DS blocks. Both follow program then linked unit order; System initialized globals are last in the initialized area, not first in DS.
System initialized global base is 0258 in SAM1 and 0266 in SAM2/3; reserve 600 vs 614 preceding initialized bytes.
A unit BSS block is omitted if nothing references it; referencing one variable retains other variables in that block.
evidence: G9 Extra must be referenced for the 164-byte block
layout_ab unused AB/BB remain with used AW/BW

statement: Interface routines return RETF and cross-unit calls use 9A; same-unit calls to far routines use PUSH CS; CALL near.
Private routines default to near under F-; F+ changes their return and adds PUSH CS at same-unit calls.
TPC /GD provides public starts and source line addresses, but no general exact routine-end table; private routines may only have line entries.

For an exact target interval, define target first, immediately follow its body with a used empty public Sentinel, and put forward helper bodies later. Account separately for target literals before its public entry.

Do not use next RET or next public as a universal extent rule: early returns, shared tails, private helpers, and literals can cross those boundaries. Use a sentinel construction or validated CFG plus literal/table ownership.
